description: We are currently building a space mission trainer
summary:
AstroRevengers
Astro Revengers is an interactive, space-learning website designed to help students explore space, understand the Moon and Mars, and prepare for future space exploration through engaging educational activities.
Key features
1. Student Login & Registration: Students can create accounts and track their individual learning progress.
2. Level Selection: Students choose Basic, Intermediate or Advanced according to their knowledge.
3. Common Space Course: Students learn foundational topics through four modules: Space, Solar System, Earth and Sun.
4. Moon & Mars Courses: Students can explore both destinations, learning about their environments, challenges, survival and future human exploration.
5. Four learning activities per module:
   - AI educational video
   - PPT presentation
   - Quiz
   - Educational game
6. Progression System: Students need at least 70% in a quiz and must complete the corresponding game before unlocking the next module.
7. VYOM AI Assistant: Helps students solve doubts and improve their weak topics, especially after unsuccessful exams.
8. Achievements & Progress Tracking: Encourages students to continue learning and monitor their performance.
Main objective
To make space education more interactive, enjoyable and practical by combining learning materials, artificial intelligence, quizzes and educational games.
Team Name: Astro Revengers
Project Vision: Making students future-ready explorers by bringing the Moon and Mars closer to the classroom.
details:
Astro Revengers – Moon & Mars Explorer

1. What does your project do and how does it work?

Astro Revengers is a space-learning website that we are developing to make learning about space more interesting and interactive for students.

Our initial idea is to create a platform where students can learn about space through different levels of education, starting from Basic and progressing towards Intermediate and Advanced.

We have started developing the frontend of our website using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Our current work includes the homepage with login and signup interfaces, a level-selection page, an About Us page and the Common Space Course.

The Common Space Course is planned to cover four topics: Space, Solar System, Earth and Sun. We have also started preparing presentations, quizzes and educational games for the learning modules.

At present, our website is still under development. Some features are designed or planned but are not yet fully functional or connected.

2. What benefits does the project have?

We believe our project can provide several benefits to students:

  • It can make learning about space more interesting and enjoyable.
  • It can help students understand space-related topics through visual and interactive learning materials.
  • Different learning levels can help students learn according to their knowledge.
  • Quizzes can help students test their understanding.
  • Educational games can make learning more engaging.
  • In the future, an AI assistant could help students understand difficult topics and improve their weak areas.

Our aim is to make space education easier to approach, especially for students who are curious about astronomy and space exploration.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main intention is to encourage students to develop an interest in space science and future space exploration.

Many students are curious about the Moon, Mars, planets and the universe, but they may not always have access to interactive learning resources.

Through Astro Revengers, we want to create a platform where students can explore these subjects in a simple, enjoyable and structured way.

In the future, we hope our project will inspire more students to learn about astronomy, science, technology and careers related to space exploration.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

The technologies and tools used in our current development include:

  • HTML: To create the structure of our website.
  • CSS: To design the website and make it visually attractive.
  • JavaScript: To add interactive elements and functionality.
  • Visual Studio Code: Our main code editor.
  • AI tools: To assist us in developing ideas, educational content and project materials.
  • Firebase: We have started setting up Firebase with the future goal of implementing student authentication and storing learning progress.

We are developing and testing the website using a computer and a web browser. We have not yet completed the backend integration.

5. How is your project creative?

Our idea is to combine space education with interactive digital learning.

Instead of creating a website that only provides written information, we want to introduce different ways of learning, such as presentations, videos, quizzes and educational games.

Some of our planned creative features include:

  • VYOM AI: A future AI assistant that will answer students' questions and help them improve in topics they find difficult.
  • Three learning levels: Basic, Intermediate and Advanced learning paths.
  • Moon and Mars exploration: Dedicated courses to help students learn about these destinations and the challenges of future human exploration.
  • Educational games: Games connected to individual learning modules.
  • Progress tracking: A system that will allow students to monitor their learning achievements.

These ideas are part of our planned development, and we aim to implement them gradually.

6. What factors did our team consider?

While planning and developing our project, we considered several important factors:

  1. Ease of use: The website should be simple for students to understand and navigate.
  2. Student engagement: Learning should be interesting rather than limited to reading textbooks.
  3. Different learning abilities: Students should have different levels according to their knowledge.
  4. Educational value: The content should encourage scientific curiosity and understanding.
  5. Future accessibility: We want the website to work on laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
  6. Future development: We want to build the project in stages and add more features as we improve our skills and technology.
  7. Innovation: We want to explore how AI and educational games can support space education.

7. Our Future Improvements

Astro Revengers is currently a work in progress. We have completed the initial frontend development and are planning several improvements.

Our future development goals include:

  • Completing Firebase authentication and student account management.
  • Connecting all webpages and improving navigation.
  • Developing the complete Common Space Course.
  • Creating dedicated Moon and Mars learning courses.
  • Adding educational AI-generated videos and presentations.
  • Developing more interactive educational games.
  • Implementing VYOM AI for doubt-solving and personalized learning assistance.
  • Adding student progress tracking, quiz results and achievements.
  • Improving the website for mobile phones, tablets and other devices.

We understand that there is still a lot of work to do, but we see this project as a starting point that we can continue developing and improving.

Conclusion

Astro Revengers is an idea built around our interest in space exploration and our desire to make space education more engaging for students.

Although our website is not yet fully functional, we have taken the first steps by developing its frontend and planning its major features.

We hope to continue improving it, learn new technologies through this process and eventually turn our idea into a complete interactive space-learning platform.

Our motto: Learn Today, Explore Tomorrow!

Team Name: Astro Revengers
